You have just finished your Operating Systems quiz, and there is a very clear area to focus on first. Your weakest topics are Processes and Memory Management. For Processes, where you missed marks on system calls, thread sharing, and deadlock conditions, try reviewing your lecture notes on process creation and the four Coffman deadlock conditions, and write out a quick summary of how threads share an address space. For Memory Management, which covers topics like external fragmentation, page faults, virtual memory, and thrashing, a great study action is to draw diagrams of paging and virtual memory to visualize how memory is allocated and when thrashing occurs. 

On the bright side, you showed a fantastic understanding of Scheduling! You got every mark in this area, correctly handling concepts like process preemption, Round Robin, and starvation. Keep up the great work with your scheduling concepts, and with a bit of targeted review on processes and memory management, you will be well prepared to boost your score next time!

You did a fantastic job on the HTTP section, earning a fully correct score! You clearly understand stateless protocols, HTTP methods, status codes like 'Not Found', and CORS. Keep up the great work with these protocol concepts.

Your current focus should be on JavaScript and HTML/CSS. Since JavaScript is your weakest area, start by reviewing variable declarations with let and const, how Promise.all handles rejections, and the differences between loose and strict equality operators. To strengthen this, try writing small code snippets in the console to test equality operators and asynchronous promises. Next, revisit HTML/CSS by reviewing block versus inline elements, such as default behaviors for divs, and practice layout styling using CSS properties that turn elements into flex containers. 

Reviewing these specific areas will help you bridge the gap between your strong HTTP knowledge and your front-end skills. Keep practicing and you will see steady improvement!
